verdict.line: You lose if Jax lands a Counter Strike or Leap Strike all-in before level 6; you win if you survive the early solo-kill window, since Nasus holds a 56% head-to-head winrate once items come online.

brief.thesis: Jax wins the lane-gold and solo-kill race because his short-cooldown E (Counter Strike) baits bad trades and his W (Empower) into Q (Leap Strike) punishes any auto-attack commitment. Nasus has no answer to that burst early, but Soul Eater lifesteal and permanent Q (Siphoning Strike) stacks mean the matchup flips once both sides hit core items, which is why Nasus sits at 56% over 109 games despite losing the laning phase on paper.

theirWindow.when: Counter Strike and Leap Strike both up
theirWindow.what: Do not auto-attack trade here — he dodges every basic attack in his E stance and stuns you for free damage, and he can close the gap with Q (Leap Strike) first. Only poke with Q (Siphoning Strike) or step on your own Spirit Fire.

yourWindow.when: right after he burns Counter Strike
yourWindow.what: He has no stun for 18/14/12/10 seconds depending on rank — commit the full trade here, landing W (Wither) the instant he closes distance so his Movement and Attack Speed bleed out before he can stack Relentless Assault (R).

start.why: 54% winrate over 87 games — the early sustain and poke-block directly answers Jax's Leap Strike pokes and Empower autos while you're still behind on trades.

boots.why: 52.5% winrate over 59 games — flat damage reduction on autos cuts into every empowered hit and every stack of his Relentless Assault (R) attack speed ramp.

core.why: Spellblade proc empowers your Q (Siphoning Strike) farm and trade damage, and the movement speed helps you avoid getting caught by Leap Strike engages.
The attack speed slow directly cripples Jax's Relentless Assault stacking and reduces the raw number of autos landing on you.
Scales your Soul Eater lifesteal and Spirit Fire sustain, while the magic resist softens Empower's bonus damage component.

situational.when: you are ahead and need to shut down his Relentless Assault (R) attack speed snowball in extended fights
he builds lifesteal or healing to survive your stacked Q
you want earlier armor and a slow proc instead of rushing full Trinity Force

runes.keystoneWhy: The heal-and-speed proc on trades lets you sustain through Jax's early poke and physically disengage before Counter Strike or Leap Strike lands, which is exactly the problem this lane presents before level 6.

summoners.why: 58.3% winrate and the most-picked combo for this matchup — Teleport lets you freeze the wave and sidestep Jax's lane-gold advantage instead of forcing bad trades, and Ghost gives you the speed to disengage from an all-in or chase him down once Counter Strike is on cooldown.

playing.title: Never trade into Counter Strike
playing.detail: If Jax's E (Counter Strike, cooldown 18/16/14/12/10s) is up, don't auto-attack him — he dodges every basic attack and stuns you back for free. Bait it with a Q (Siphoning Strike) poke first.

playing.title: Farm Q over fighting
playing.detail: Prioritize landing Q (Siphoning Strike) last-hits on its 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown over forcing trades — every stack is permanent damage that eventually outscales his flat kit.

playing.title: Save Wither for his leap
playing.detail: Hold W (Wither) and land it the instant he commits Q (Leap Strike) at you — it decelerates his Movement and Attack Speed, stopping him from stacking Relentless Assault (R) after he sticks.

playing.title: Play passive levels 3-5
playing.detail: His solo-kill rate peaks once Counter Strike comes online around level 3 — don't contest CS into his cooldowns, just absorb the pressure.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire on his Empower
playing.detail: When he goes for a W (Empower) auto, place E (Spirit Fire) under him — the armor reduction flips the follow-up trade in your favor instead of his.

playing.title: All-in once his E is down
playing.detail: After he burns Counter Strike he has no stun for up to 18 seconds — commit fully here, especially from level 6 onward with R (Fury of the Sands) up.

playing.title: Rush to Trinity Force
playing.detail: You lose the solo-kill race pre-items — Trinity Force into Frozen Heart is the point where your 56% head-to-head record actually starts to show.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured Nasus vs Jax games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the cooldown timing and trade-window reasoning is my own tactical read layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Pay attention to Jax’s (P) and Conqueror stack count while keeping your distance. Focus foremost on farming with [Q], and use Wither [W] to create some distance when Jax closes in.
